summary: Dagmar Schwerk works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at the University of Hamburg from circa 2010 to 2017, completing her doctorate under supervisor Dorji Wangchuk around 2012 to 2017.

Dagpo Rinpoche is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Tenzin Gyatso, Ngawang Nyima, Thubten Lungtog Tenzin Trinley, and Trijang Rinpoche, and taught David Seyfort Ruegg, Anne-Marie Blondeau, Thoupten Phuntshog, and Marie-Stella Boussemart.
Daichi Tado works in Buddhist studies. In 2020, he was attested as a part-time lecturer (非常勤講師) at both Waseda University and the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies.

Daiei Kaneko was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Otani University (circa 1901–1904) under Manshi Kiyozawa. He founded Koho Gakuen and held academic posts at Otani University (~1925–1951) and Toyo University (~1926–1928).

Daiju Sasaki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University. In 2015, he held posts as a part-time lecturer at Taisho University and as a full-time lecturer in sectarian studies at Chisan Denpōin.

Daijō Tokiwa specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology, studying at the University of Tokyo under Tetsujiro Inoue and Yujiro Motora. He held professorships at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University, and served at the Academy of Oriental Culture.

Dainin Katagiri was a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar who studied at Eihei-ji and Komazawa University. He served at the Zenshuji Soto Mission and San Francisco Zen Center, and founded the Minnesota Zen Meditation Center and Hokyoji Zen Practice Community.

Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Waseda University and the University of Tokyo under Soyen Shaku. He held professorships at Gakushuin University, Otani University, and Columbia University.

Daishun Ueyama works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. He studied under Akira Fujieda (~1957–1962) and served as an assistant professor (~1970–1978) and later president (1983) at Ryukoku University.

Daito Shimaji was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Educated at Ryukoku and Toyo Universities, he taught at Toyo University (~1906–1927), the University of Tokyo (1923), Rissho University (~1924–1927), and Komazawa University (~1925–1927).

Dale S. Wright specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Alan Anderson, Wang Pachow, and Robert Scharlemann, and served as Gamble Professor of Religious Studies and Asian Studies at Occidental College from circa 1980 to 2018.

Dalsukh Malvania was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied under Sukhlal Sanghvi. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (~1940–1957) and served as Director of the Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Institute of Indology (~1957–1978).
Damchö Gyatso studied under Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse, Penor Rinpoche, and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Damdin Badaraev was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics who studied under Bidia Dandaron and George de Roerich.

Damien Keown is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who earned his D.Phil. at Oxford. He founded the Journal of Buddhist Ethics and taught at Goldsmiths, University of London (~1986–2013), where he became Emeritus Professor.
Damodar was an Indology scholar who served as Head Pandit at Maharaja's High School in Srinagar and at Maharaja's Pathashala, Srinagar (attested 1892).

Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi was an Indologist and historian who studied at Harvard. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University, Aligarh Muslim University, Fergusson College, and was a mathematics professor at the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (1945–1962).

Dan Arnold is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago. He taught at McGill University and served as an assistant professor at the University of Chicago Divinity School.

Dan Lusthaus is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his Ph.D. at Temple University. He held positions at Grinnell College, Bates College, Florida State University, the University of Georgia, and Harvard University.

Dan Martin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his Ph.D. from Indiana University. He held posts at the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and Carnegie Mellon University.
